pr_title: cgroup: Add support for ProtectControlGroups= private and strict
pr_body:
This PR adds two settings private and strict to the ProtectControlGroups= property. Private will unshare the cgroup namespace and mount a read-write private cgroup2 filesystem at /sys/fs/cgroup. Strict does the same except the mount is read-only. Since the unit is running in a cgroup namespace, the new root of /sys/fs/cgroup is the unit's own cgroup.

We also add a new dbus property ProtectControlGroupsEx which accepts strings instead of boolean. This will allow users to use private/strict via dbus and systemd-run in addition to service files.

Note private and strict are ignored if kernel doesn't support cgroup2 or system is not using unified hierarchy.

Fixes: [#34634](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/34634)

issue_context.title: Add PrivateControlGroups= setting to service units
issue_context.body:
### Component

systemd

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

Meta is migrating its Twine container engine to use systemd transient units for spawning containers - we already do use it in a limited way. Our current container engine currently enforces all containers use cgroup namespaces - our whole fleet is cgroup v2.

### Describe the solution you'd like

To do so, we need support for cgroup namespaces. To do so, we propose adding a PrivateControlGroups setting (similar to PrivateMounts)

This would do the following in order:
1. Unshare cgroup namespace
2. Mount a private mount of /sys/fs/cgroup (instead of bind mount from host)

On cgroup v1, this setting would be ignored.

Open question: /sys and sub-mounts are currently bind mounted from host for service units. If PrivateControlGroups is set, should we also mount private versions of /sys and all sub-mounts rather than use a bind mount?

cc @anitazha @DaanDeMeyer 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Why not nspawn:
1. nspawn is opinionated (for good reason) on container setup. Twine containers have a variety of settings that are needed for customization of Twine containers e.g. ExtraFileDescriptors: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/34556
2. nspawn is only a CLI, our Twine agent team prefers API

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

_No response_
comments: Note that we currently have fields ProtectControlGroups=, ControlGroup=, ControlGroupId=. Hence the new setting should be called PrivateControlGroups= I guess.

> Open question: /sys and sub-mounts are currently bind mounted from host for service units. If PrivateCgroups is set, should we also mount private versions of /sys and all sub-mounts rather than use a bind mount?

I don't see a reason to do this. (At least none related to CLONE_NEWCGROUP. There are valid ones regarding CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_NEWNET I guess, but I don't think CLONE_NEWCGROUP should necessarily trigger this)

> ###
> 
> Why not nspawn:
> 
>     1. nspawn is opinionated (for good reason) on container setup. Twine containers have a variety of settings that are needed for customization of Twine containers e.g. ExtraFileDescriptors:

So I agree with this. I think we should rework nspawn eventually to be just a different frontend for regular service management.

@poettering I noticed we have a ProtectControlGroups setting...it might be a bit confusing for the user to have 2 settings - ProtectControlGroups and PrivateControlGroups - control how /sys/fs/cgroup is mounted.

Another approach might be like ProtectSystem which allows yes, no, full and strict. ProtectHome also does something similar: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.exec.html#ProtectHome=

So for ProtectControlGroups we could do:
1. no - /sys/fs/cgroup used from host (current behavior)
2. yes - /sys/fs/cgroup bind mounted from host read-only (current behavior)
3. private - /sys/fs/cgroup has read-write private mount within mount namespace
4. private-read-only - /sys/fs/cgroup has read-only private mount within mount namespace

This solution has the added benefit that the backend is cleaner as opposed to passing two booleans around. But we would need to migrate from boolean dbus API -> string e.g. ProtectControlGroupsEx. And private-read-only is a little verbose...

Let me know what you think! Fine to do 2 properties as well, we can have the two boolean dbus properties merge into one enum field in execute.c

idea sounds good. We have been doing something similar for other PrivateXYZ= and ProectXYZ= knobs.

I'd probably find a different name for `private-read-only` though. Maybe `strict` or so?

I must say I liked the conceptual distinction between Protect* and Private* directives. The former standing for the system being protected from the service, the latter meaning service has it own (restricted) view of the structures (which possibly _also_ protects the broad system). I could reason about what each directive means just by looking at a unit file without delving into manpages and reading a case breakdown for special values.

I guess I'm gonna live with the new approach. Is this the systematization that holds?

| Private*= | Protect*= | New Protect*= |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no | no | no |
| no | yes | yes |
| yes | no | private |
| yes | yes | strict |

review_comments: the conditionalization left of the first && seems unnecessary?
I.e. callers of a getter could potentially trigger a warning log, which seems absurd. Let's just document this and fall back gracefully. Might as well leave a TODO for removal in v258.
Fallback is already documented in xml files and comments. Will leave a TODO

When this mount option is added? If this is added in 5.2 or newer, then assuming not supported is OK, but if not, I think it is better to assume it is supported.
Please add a comment when it is added.

Also is `nsdelegate` mount option always supported when CLONE_NEWCGROUP is supported?
If not, we need to also check the mount option.

memory_recursiveprot is added in 5.7 so we need to check: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/25834

nsdelegate has been since 4.13 so no need to check: https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewtopic.php?id=230777

Will add a comment for both
